_about: Hand-edited message copy (not generated). startChecked: which reasons begin checked. local: the state sentence, checked by default. responsibilities: optional sentence for members with leadership or committee roles, keyed by the member's name in data.json.

local.AZ: Here in Arizona, Representatives Ansari and Grijalva are cosponsoring the Ban ASI Act.
local.CA: Here in California, SB 53 has required transparency from frontier AI developers since January 2026, and a new state report recommends standby authority to cap recursive self-improvement. Please protect state laws like this from federal preemption.
local.CO: Here in Colorado, the Colorado AI Act already sets rules for AI used in high-stakes decisions. States are acting, and Congress should too.
local.GA: Here in Georgia, DeKalb County has paused new data centers, and a state bill would halt new permits until March 2027. Families here are worried about power bills.
local.IL: Here in Illinois, the AI Safety Act now requires annual independent audits of the largest frontier AI developers. That should be the national floor.
local.IN: Here in Indiana, Bloomington voted this month to ban superintelligence development until the state adopts a safety framework. Communities want limits, and Congress should set them nationally.
local.KS: Here in Kansas, our governor-elect ran on a moratorium on new AI data centers. People here want a say in how far and how fast AI goes.
local.KY: Here in Kentucky, the debate over an AI kill switch has come down to getting the facts first. Independent testing would give Congress those facts.
local.LA: Here in Louisiana, Senator Kennedy wrote the AI Emergency Button Act and has warned on the Senate floor about AI that improves itself.
local.ME: Here in Maine, the legislature voted for a moratorium on large data centers through November 2027. Mainers want AI to grow on terms we set.
local.MD: Here in Maryland, lawmakers have weighed data center moratoriums, and Senator Van Hollen has led calls for a US–China pause and a ban on recursive self-improvement.
local.MA: Here in Massachusetts, a frontier AI safety bill is before the legislature. Federal rules should set a floor, not wipe out state protections.
local.MI: Here in Michigan, the state Senate passed a chatbot age-verification bill, and a frontier AI bill is pending. Michiganders want guardrails.
local.MN: Here in Minnesota, a bill would pause new data centers over 100 megawatts. Minnesotans want AI to grow on terms we set.
local.MO: Here in Missouri, the legislature sent the governor a ban on AI therapy chatbots, and Senator Hawley has led on holding AI companies accountable.
local.NH: Here in New Hampshire, Governor Ayotte called for a data center moratorium and won re-election. Limits on AI are popular across party lines.
local.NY: Here in New York, the RAISE Act's frontier AI rules take effect on January 1, 2027, and the state has paused new large data centers for a year. Please make RAISE-style oversight the national standard.
local.NC: Here in North Carolina, our senator-elect wants data centers to pay the full cost of their energy so families don't foot the bill.
local.OK: Here in Oklahoma, lawmakers debated a data center moratorium this year. How fast AI grows matters here too.
local.PA: Here in Pennsylvania, bills would pause new data centers for three years and let towns say no to them. People want local control over AI's footprint.
local.SC: Here in South Carolina, our senator-elect, a pediatrician, has called for a two-year pause on new data centers.
local.SD: Here in South Dakota, lawmakers debated a one-year data center moratorium this year. How fast AI grows matters here too.
local.TX: Here in Texas, our governor-elect campaigned on a data center moratorium, and Texans in Congress from both parties have introduced bills on superintelligence and an AI kill switch.
local.VT: Here in Vermont, a bill would ban new data center projects through July 2030. Vermonters want a say before the AI build-out reaches us.
local.VA: Here in Virginia, lawmakers are weighing a data center moratorium while the grid catches up. AI's growth is already straining our infrastructure.
local.WI: Here in Wisconsin, Port Washington voters demanded a say on big incentives after a $15 billion AI campus was announced. People want accountability for what gets built.
